# Package lookup • 3.20.0

In the ordinary 3.20 basic search, Module mode has priority and Config is the fallback. MODULE disables that fallback. CMAKE_FIND_PACKAGE_PREFER_CONFIG can reverse the ordinary priority.

# Package lookup • 3.28.0

From 3.24 even Module-mode calls first check the redirects directory. FetchContent redirection bypasses ordinary searching and ignores component information. Without redirection the basic signature normally tries Module before Config. MODULE disallows ordinary Config fallback.

Under the documented component conventions, a required component that is missing makes the package unavailable. Adding REQUIRED makes that failure fatal. An optional missing component can coexist with a successful find.

REGISTRY_VIEW and GLOBAL arrived in 3.24. Registry views are meaningful only on Windows. GLOBAL promotes imported targets to global scope in the importing project.

BYPASS_PROVIDER is reserved for a dependency provider calling the built-in finder directly, so its own request does not return to that provider.

# Timestamp formatting • 3.20.0

In 3.20 TIMESTAMP writes a formatted date/time, yielding an empty string if unavailable. Unknown format codes are copied literally. SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH overrides the current time and the UTC default format ends in Z.

# Timestamp formatting • 3.28.0

TIMESTAMP normally uses local time. UTC requests UTC representation. If obtaining the timestamp fails, the result is empty. Unknown format codes are copied literally. SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, when set, supplies the time instead of the current clock.

The %f field, introduced in 3.23, is the microsecond within the second, 000000 through 999999. %U permits week 00; ISO week %V, added in 3.22, ranges from 01 to 53.

From 3.26 %z prints a signed hours-and-minutes offset and %Z gives the zone name. Without an explicit format, a UTC timestamp has a trailing Z and a local timestamp has none.

# Configure-time pipelines • 3.28.0

The command runs at configure time. Multiple COMMAND clauses in one invocation form a concurrent pipeline. For sequential steps use separate invocations. Standard output feeds the next input; standard error is shared.

TIMEOUT accepts seconds including fractions. Expiry terminates unfinished children and leaves a timeout string in RESULT_VARIABLE. The singular result describes the last child, and RESULTS_VARIABLE records each child in command order.

COMMAND_ERROR_IS_FATAL ANY stops on failure by any child. LAST stops only on failure of the final child, so a failure limited to an earlier stage is not fatal under LAST.

# Configure-time file operations • 3.28.0

RENAME normally replaces the destination atomically within a filesystem. From 3.21 NO_REPLACE preserves an existing destination. With RESULT, that collision stores NO_REPLACE; success stores 0.

COPY_FILE, added in 3.21, copies file contents. Directories are unsupported. ONLY_IF_DIFFERENT preserves an equal destination's timestamp. Copying does not create a reconfigure dependency on the input.

From 3.26 INPUT_MAY_BE_RECENT enables a few retries on Windows when permission to read a newly made input is denied. The option is meaningful only on Windows.

REAL_PATH defaults to the current source directory for relative inputs. EXPAND_TILDE first consults USERPROFILE on Windows, falling back to HOME. Elsewhere it uses HOME alone. Under 3.28's CMP0152 new behavior symlinks are resolved before parent components are collapsed.

# Installation rules • 3.28.0

Relative install destinations use CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX. Absolute destinations are taken as written; CPack installer generators do not support absolute destinations.

A full installation includes components unless a rule is marked EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL. Such a rule may still be installed in a component-specific run. The default component name is Unspecified and can be configured with CMAKE_INSTALL_DEFAULT_COMPONENT_NAME.

Relative install(SCRIPT) input paths use the current source directory. Script code runs during installation. ALL_COMPONENTS, available from 3.21, runs the script for every component of a component-specific installation and is mutually exclusive with COMPONENT.

# Generated build steps • 3.28.0

APPEND extends an existing rule's commands and dependencies. When the original output is a generator expression it need only match in one configuration.
The appended work then applies in all configurations. APPEND ignores COMMENT, MAIN_DEPENDENCY and WORKING_DIRECTORY.

A relative byproduct path is relative to the corresponding build directory. In 3.28 under the documented CMP0154 behavior for targets using file sets, byproducts are private except those in non-private file sets.

COMMENT supplies a build-time message shown before execution. Starting in 3.26 that message may use generator expressions.

JOB_SERVER_AWARE was introduced in 3.28. For Unix, MSYS and MinGW Makefiles, enabling it prefixes the recipe with +. Other generators silently ignore it.

# Deferred calls and diagnostics • 3.28.0

The default defer point is the end of the current directory. A return does not cancel a scheduled call. Ordinary variable references in deferred arguments are resolved when the call runs.

A DIRECTORY for DEFER must be known and still processing. Either its source or binary directory can identify it. A relative directory is interpreted from the current source directory.

Within the selected directory GET_CALL returns the first matching scheduled call, with arguments unevaluated. CANCEL_CALL removes all calls with a matching ID and ignores an unknown ID.

GET_MESSAGE_LOG_LEVEL, added in 3.25, writes the effective level to a variable. The command-line log level outranks CMAKE_MESSAGE_LOG_LEVEL. When neither is set the result is the default level.

# Target source sets • 3.28.0

PRIVATE and PUBLIC source items populate SOURCES for the target build. PUBLIC and INTERFACE populate INTERFACE_SOURCES for dependents. A custom target only accepts PRIVATE scope. Calls on the same target append in call order.

File sets arrived in 3.23. The CXX_MODULES type arrived in 3.28 for interface module and partition sources. It cannot have INTERFACE scope except on an imported target.

On initial creation with BASE_DIRS omitted, the current source directory becomes a base. Explicit relative bases are relative to that source directory.
No base of the same set may be nested under another, even if specified in different calls.

Files in HEADERS sets have HEADER_FILE_ONLY enabled. PUBLIC and INTERFACE file sets are eligible for installation and export.
